extracted.intended_audience: Users of the Magma computer algebra system and mathematicians working in combinatorial design theory and finite geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and reference for constructing, manipulating, and testing combinatorial designs, difference sets, and finite (projective/affine) planes in Magma, including related graph/code conversions and group/automorphism operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witt and Hadamard design constructors
rubrics_metrics.description: WittDesign(n) constructs the small and large Mathieu (Witt) designs for n = 12 and n = 24 respectively; related functions include IsHadamard(M), IsHadamardEquivalent(H,J), HadamardRowDesign(H,i), HadamardColumnDesign(H,i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WittDesign(12) returns a 5-(12,6,1) design; WittDesign(24) returns a 5-(24,8,1) design. HadamardRowDesign(H,i) and HadamardColumnDesign(H,i) construct Hadamard 3-designs corresponding to a row or column of an n×n Hadamard matrix (n ≥ 4). IsHadamard tests whether a matrix has ±1 entries and satisfies M*M^t = n I_n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hadamard matrix definition and test
rubrics_metrics.description: A matrix M is Hadamard if all entries are ±1 and M * M^t = m I_m for an m×m matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use IsHadamard(M) to test the property. Hadamard matrices are used to build 3-designs via HadamardRowDesign and HadamardColumnDesign; IsHadamardEquivalent(H,J) tests equivalence of Hadamard matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference set definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A (v,k,λ)-difference set for a group G of order v is a k-subset D of G such that the multiset {g h^{-1} : g,h ∈ D, g ≠ h} contains every non-identity element of G exactly λ times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Difference sets are used to generate incidence structures via the development process (translate the difference set by each group element to form blocks). The universe (group) may be represented additively (residue class ring or abelian group) or multiplicatively (finite group).

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference set and development functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions: DifferenceSet(p,t), SingerDifferenceSet(n,q), IsDifferenceSet(B), Development(B), Development(T).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DifferenceSet(p,t) constructs difference sets of type string t (t in {"Q","H6","T","B","B0","O","O0","W4"}) with imposed conditions on p. SingerDifferenceSet(n,q) produces a Singer difference set corresponding to a hyperplane of PG(n,q). IsDifferenceSet(B) returns true and λ if B is a difference set over ZZ/mZZ or an iterable finite group. Development(B) returns the symmetric design with point set A (the group) whose blocks are the translates of B. Development(T) takes a difference family T = {B1,...,Bl} and returns the incidence structure whose ith block is (B1 ∪ ... ∪ Bl) translated by the ith element of A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing difference sets via group orbits and multipliers
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiplier theorems restrict a difference set, one can construct candidate sets by grouping orbits of a mapping (e.g., x ↦ 2x) in a residue class ring and testing them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute orbits of the permutation induced by the multiplier on the ambient set; form unions of orbits whose sizes match required k, then test with IsDifferenceSet. Example: in ZZ/21ZZ multiplier 2 forces 2D = D, so D is union of orbits under x→2x.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective and affine plane axioms (for construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projective plane criteria: any two distinct points lie on a unique line, any two lines meet in a unique point, and there exist four points no three collinear. Affine plane criteria: any two distinct points lie on a unique line, given a line l and point P not on l there is a unique parallel through P, and there exist three non-collinear points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When building a plane from incidence data the lines must satisfy these axioms; Magma provides constructors ProjectivePlane<point-set | line-set> and AffinePlane<point-set | line-set> that interpret the right-hand side in several forms (incidence matrix, set of codewords via supports, or explicit list of line subsets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supported forms for plane constructors
rubrics_metrics.description: The line-set in the constructors ProjectivePlane and AffinePlane may be given as a v×b 0/1 incidence matrix, as a set of codewords (supports become lines), or as a comma-separated list of subsets/lines/sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points may be specified explicitly as an indexed set V of v points or by the integer v (V = {@1,...,v@}). Use these flexible input forms depending on the source of your data (matrix, code, or listed lines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructor Check parameter
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructors ProjectivePlane and AffinePlane accept a parameter Check which defaults to true to validate the axioms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set Check := false to skip validation (saves time for large planes or when data is known correct); but the user is then responsible for ensuring the structure satisfies the plane axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planes from incidence structures
rubrics_metrics.description: If an incidence structure I (in any incidence category) has the properties of an affine or projective plane, it may be converted to category PlaneAﬀ or PlaneProj using AffinePlane(I) or ProjectivePlane(I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows reuse of previously-built incidence structures; the function assumes I satisfies plane axioms (or will check if Check default is true).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classical planes from vector spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Desarguesian (classical) projective and affine planes arise from vector spaces over finite fields: ProjectivePlane(W), ProjectivePlane(F), ProjectivePlane(q) (similarly AffinePlane). Points/lines printed in normalized coordinate form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projective PG(2,q) uses 3-colon coordinates (a:b:c) interpreted as ax+by+cz=0; affine AG(2,q) uses (a,b) and lines <a:b:c> as ax+by+c=0. Some Magma operations are only available for classical planes; coordinates for projective points normalized so leftmost non-zero coordinate is 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality and isomorphism semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: eq and ne test equality of incidence structures/planes by requiring the same underlying point set and identical blocks/lines. IsIsomorphic(I,J) tests isomorphism (weaker than equality) and, if true, returns an explicit mapping from I to J.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use IsIsomorphic to detect structural equivalence even when representations differ; a true result returns the mapping that demonstrates the isomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automorphism group functions and transitivity tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions: AutomorphismGroup(I), PointGroup(I), BlockGroup(I), IsPointTransitive(I), IsBlockTransitive(I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AutomorphismGroup(I) returns the automorphism group: if I is simple it acts on the point-set; otherwise it acts on the union of the point-set and block-set (so group degree is number_of_points + number_of_blocks). PointGroup and BlockGroup give actions on points and blocks. IsPointTransitive/IsBlockTransitive test transitivity. The automorphism functions can return additional data (e.g., generators) and can be investigated (FactoredOrder, SylowSubgroup, Orbit, Image, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incidence structures, graphs, and linear codes relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions: IncidenceStructure(G), PointGraph(I), BlockGraph(I), IncidenceGraph(I), LinearCode(I,K). These convert between graphs, incidence structures, and linear codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IncidenceStructure(G) makes an incidence structure corresponding to a graph G (blocks correspond to edges). PointGraph(I), BlockGraph(I) create graphs from incidence structures. LinearCode(I,K) returns the linear code over field K generated by characteristic functions of blocks. Sets of codewords (supports) can be used to form incidence structures; e.g., the code over GF(2) generated by the Fano plane is isomorphic to the Hamming code with r=3 (IsIsomorphic can confirm).

rubrics_metrics.name: Point-set and line-set operations and representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions: IncidenceMatrix(P), PointSet(P), LineSet(P), Points(P), Lines(P), NumberOfPoints(P), NumberOfLines(P), Support(P), Rep(V), Random(V), Rep(L), Random(L), ParentPlane(x), V.i, L.i, V!x, L!S, Set(l), Support(l).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point-set V and line-set L are special categories PlanePtSet and PlaneLnSet; Points(P) and Lines(P) return indexed sets of points/lines. Support(P) returns the underlying objects (vectors or integers) that created points. Use V!x to coerce support elements to points; use L!S to obtain the unique line containing a set S of collinear points. Distinguish Set(l) (returns points as plane points) and Support(l) (returns original-category elements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrency, collinearity, and parallelism operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions: IsCollinear(P,S), IsConcurrent(P,S), Pencil(P,p), ContainsQuadrangle(P,S), IsParallel(P,l,m), ParallelClass(P,l), ParallelClasses(P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IsCollinear returns whether points of S are collinear and, if true, the line; IsConcurrent tests whether lines in S are concurrent and returns the common point if so. Pencil(P,p) returns all lines through p. ContainsQuadrangle(P,S) tests for a quadrangle. For affine planes IsParallel detects parallel lines; ParallelClass and ParallelClasses give line partitions by parallelism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classical plane coordinate functions and normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions: VectorSpace(P), Field(P), V![a,b,c], V![a,b], Eltseq(p), Coordinates(P,p), p[i], L![a,b,c], Eltseq(l), Coordinates(P,l), l[i], L![m,b], Slope(l).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These convert between plane points/lines and vectors/coordinate sequences over the underlying field. For projective planes coordinates are normalized so the leftmost nonzero entry is 1; multiple non-zero scalar multiples of a vector represent the same projective point (use VP ! [a,b,c] to coerce and Eltseq to read normalized coordinates). For affine planes vectors map one-to-one to points and slope/line forms are available for AG2(K).

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical invariants and properties of a plane
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions: Order(P), pRank(P,p), pRank(P), IsDesarguesian(P), IsSelfDual(P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order(P) returns n such that a projective plane has n^2+n+1 points and lines and n+1 points per line; for affine planes order n gives n^2 points, n^2+n lines, n points per line and n+1 lines through each point. IsDesarguesian(P) tests if P is Desarguesian (true for classical planes). IsSelfDual tests whether a projective plane is isomorphic to its dual. pRank functions compute the p-rank invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subplane construction and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructor sub< P | points specification > builds the smallest subplane of P containing a given set T of points (specified as points/sets/sequences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For projective planes T must contain a quadrangle (four points with no three collinear); for affine planes T must contain three non-collinear points. SubfieldSubplane(P, F) constructs a subplane by taking points whose coordinates lie in subfield F (for classical planes). Points of the subplane may be coerced into the larger plane automatically.
